name: Dovetail
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repos
verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Dovetail, store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository. The hard boundary is media transcription, participant data, integrations, governance, and collaboration scale, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: collect structured feedback for store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status or research view
whatYouLose: media transcription, participant data, integrations, governance, and collaboration scale
moatType: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Dovetail because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Team plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Dovetail in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect structured feedback for store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status or research view
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
